{
  "research_question": "Does stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) significantly affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level categorical factor",
    "For Success (binary), use logistic regression or chi-square test of independence rather than ANOVA, or treat as proportion and use beta regression if appropriate",
    "Given the large sample sizes per group (n=3,505 to 48,846), the F-test will be highly powered; focus on effect sizes (eta-squared or partial eta-squared) alongside p-values",
    "Check for homogeneity of variance using Levene's test; if violated, use Welch's ANOVA",
    "For non-normal residuals (likely given bounded variables like Path Efficiency and AD), consider robust ANOVA or permutation-based alternatives"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "Perform pairwise comparisons between all 10 pairs of stimulation paradigms for each continuous outcome",
    "Use Tukey's HSD for balanced designs or Games-Howell for unequal variances/unequal sample sizes",
    "For Success (binary), use pairwise z-tests for proportions with multiple comparison correction",
    "Prioritize comparisons of Sham vs. active stimulation conditions (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) as these address the primary experimental question",
    "Report effect sizes (Cohen's d for continuous variables, odds ratios for Success) alongside adjusted p-values"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control for the 10 pairwise comparisons per outcome, applied separately to each of the 5 response variables; familywise error rate controlled at alpha=0.05. Given the exploratory nature of secondary comparisons, FDR is preferred over Bonferroni to balance Type I and Type II error rates.",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Multinomial logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as the categorical response variable and the five performance metrics as predictors. This is the appropriate choice because: (1) Stim Paradigm is categorical with 5 unordered levels, making ordinary linear regression inappropriate; (2) the performance variables are continuous and can serve as features; (3) multinomial logistic regression directly models the probability of each stimulation condition given performance characteristics. Alternative: Random forest classifier or gradient boosting (XGBoost/LightGBM) for non-linear relationships and feature interactions, with 5-fold cross-validation to assess generalization. Given the class imbalance (Combined: 48,846 vs Sham: 3,505), use stratified sampling and evaluate with balanced accuracy or macro-averaged F1 rather than raw accuracy.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Assumed based on experimental design; verify no temporal autocorrelation within mice",
    "Normality: QQ-plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests on residuals; likely violations given bounded variables (Path Efficiency, AD, Success)",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test; likely violated given vastly different sample sizes and visual inspection of means (Sham SD likely differs from Combined)",
    "Multicollinearity among predictors: Check VIF in multinomial logistic regression; Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target may correlate",
    "Complete separation check in multinomial logistic regression: Sham appears distinct on all metrics, may cause convergence issues",
    "Sample size adequacy: Rule of thumb of 10-20 observations per parameter; satisfied given n=76,655"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham will show significantly lower Success (0.273 vs 0.673-0.785), higher Time-to-Target (4.68s vs 2.56-3.14s), lower Path Efficiency (0.308 vs 0.432-0.504), lower Average Speed (10.74 vs 11.97-12.83), and lower AD (0.236 vs 0.336-0.399) compared to all active stimulation conditions",
    "Combined stimulation will show the highest Success rate (0.780) and fastest Time-to-Target (2.56s), suggesting synergistic benefit of multimodal stimulation",
    "Bright Visual Only will outperform Dim Visual Only on Success (0.785 vs 0.673) and Time-to-Target (2.61s vs 3.14s), indicating intensity-dependent visual effects",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only will perform similarly, with intermediate outcomes between Sham and Combined/Bright Visual",
    "AD will be highest in Combined (0.399) and Bright Visual (0.387), lowest in Sham (0.236), suggesting angular dispersion tracks with active engagement/alertness"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe class imbalance in Stim Paradigm (Combined: 63.7% of data, Sham: 4.6%) will reduce precision of estimates for underrepresented conditions and may bias predictive models toward the majority class",
    "No mouse-level identifiers in analysis: Cannot account for within-mouse clustering or individual differences; violates independence assumption if multiple trials per mouse",
    "No temporal information: Cannot assess learning effects or trial order effects",
    "Success is binary but analyzed alongside continuous variables; mixed data types complicate multivariate approaches",
    "Path Efficiency shows extreme range (max=29.8) suggesting outliers or calculation artifacts that may influence parametric tests",
    "Single dataset replication (Run 287, Replication 3) limits generalizability; no assessment of run-to-run variability",
    "Temperature=0.25 and specific prompt template may affect model behavior if LLM-generated labels are involved, though this appears to be mouse behavioral data"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Mixed-effects models (multilevel models) with Mouse as random intercept to account for within-mouse clustering, followed by Bayesian multinomial logistic regression with weakly informative priors to handle class imbalance and provide uncertainty quantification for predictive classification of stimulation paradigm from performance profiles."
}
